title: Disambiguate proxy-synthesized 404 from real upstream 404
answers: External AM sync drops a real fetch failure as 'no upstream config'
How to tell a Grafana datasource-proxy error 404 apart from Mimir's real 404
Why is a misconfigured/unloaded plugin silently treated as 'no alertmanager config'?
body: Symptom: when a fetch is routed through Grafana's datasource proxy, a 404 can mean either the real upstream's 'no config for this tenant' (Mimir's plain-text 404) or a proxy-level failure such as a missing/unloaded plugin, which the proxy itself returns via ReqContext.JsonApiErr as a JSON {"message":...} body. Treating both the same way misclassifies real failures as the harmless case. Root cause/fix: external_am_syncer.go:fetchMimirConfig calls proxyErrorMessage to check whether the 404 body parses as the proxy's JSON envelope — if so, it's a real fetch error; otherwise it's Mimir's genuine empty-config 404 and maps to errNoUpstreamConfig. Constraints: this heuristic is specific to responses that pass through Grafana's own JsonApiErr; reuse it (or the dsproxyclient.Result.Body) whenever another syncer classifies a proxied upstream status code as a benign 'not configured' outcome.
applies: ngalert syncers (and similar background fetchers) interpreting status codes returned by a response routed through the datasource proxy.
says: Alertmanager sync treats real fetch failures as harmless config absence
How to distinguish Grafana datasource proxy 404 from upstream 404?
Why is a misconfigured plugin silently treated as missing configuration?
Datasource proxy error responses look identical to empty upstream config
When does a 404 mean real failure versus empty configuration?
search: When a fetch is routed through Grafana's datasource proxy, disambiguate a 404 from the proxy's own error (JSON {"message":...} via ReqContext.JsonApiErr) versus a genuine upstream 'no config' (Mimir's plain-text 404) by checking whether the response body parses as the proxy's JSON envelope. If the 404 body is JSON, it signals a proxy-level failure (missing/unloaded plugin); otherwise it maps to errNoUpstreamConfig. This heuristic is specific to proxy responses and reuse it when another syncer classifies a proxied upstream status code as a benign 'not configured' outcome. Applies to ngalert syncers and similar background fetchers interpreting status codes routed through the datasource proxy (pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/external_am_syncer.go:fetchMimirConfig, proxyErrorMessage, dsproxyclient.Result.Body).
